items.summary: IBM Granite introduces a default ensemble interface to simplify time-series forecasting by combining four pre-trained models without requiring dataset-specific training or manual selection. The system offers two aggregation recipes: a Probabilistic Ensemble using uniform probability pooling and an IQR Ensemble weighting members by forecast spread. Evaluated on the GIFT-Eval benchmark as of October 20, 2026, the ensemble outperformed individual models on aggregate metrics, with the Probabilistic Ensemble achieving a MASE of 0.683. While the ensemble provides robust, consistent results across diverse series, it does not guarantee calibration under distribution shifts and may increase inference time due to loading multiple checkpoints.
items.title: IBM Granite Offers Default Ensemble for Time-Series Forecasting

items.summary: NVIDIA is enabling European retailers to adopt open models and physical intelligence across various operations. Shopify reduced inference costs by 90% and improved response speeds using NVIDIA-accelerated models for its AI assistant. Zooplus rebuilt its product discovery stack to achieve 86% search accuracy. Photoroom standardized images for Vestiaire Collective, increasing listing liquidity by 5%. Omi accelerated 3D asset generation for L'Oréal by 10x. Mirakl runs open models to maintain technology sovereignty. Otto Group advanced its autonomous warehouse in Haldensleben, Germany, using NVIDIA Omniverse. Additionally, CATCHES improved conversion rates by 55% through its RealFit deployment. These initiatives demonstrate NVIDIA's role in advancing retail efficiency and innovation through simulation and AI.
items.title: NVIDIA Powers European Retailers with Open Models and Physical Intelligence

items.summary: NVIDIA has deployed open AI models, including StormScope EU, to support weather and climate prediction across Europe. These tools, running on NVIDIA computing, utilize satellite observations to provide detailed regional forecasts updated every 10 minutes. Organizations like AXA, Vaisala Xweather, and the University of Manchester are adapting these models for risk assessment, lightning data integration, and air-quality modeling, demonstrating the technology's versatility for specialized environmental challenges.
items.title: NVIDIA Earth-2 Models Deployed Across Europe for Weather and Climate Prediction

items.summary: Google is facing widespread anger in Finland after illegally clearing approximately 250,000 trees near Muhos to build a datacentre. The Finnish Licensing and Supervision Authority ordered a temporary work stoppage due to missing environmental impact assessments. While Google's country manager apologized, citing a misunderstanding of legislation, conservationists condemn the action as 'pure arrogance.' The incident has sparked national debate over the role of datacentres in Finland's energy strategy and prompted over 93,000 people to sign a petition demanding stricter regulations and compensation for local communities.
items.title: Google faces anger in Finland after illegal tree felling for datacentre

items.summary: Anthropic announced that its latest Claude models will include AI text watermarks to comply with the EU AI Act, effective August 2026. The watermarking technology, based on Google DeepMind's SynthID-Text, uses steganography to subtly alter word choices without changing meaning or consuming extra tokens. Major providers like OpenAI and Google are also implementing similar measures. While the watermark helps detect AI-generated content, it cannot identify the specific user account. Anthropic lists several affected models, including Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, noting that all outputs across platforms will carry the watermark.
items.title: Anthropic Adds AI Watermarks to Latest Models Amid EU Regulations

items.summary: SGX Group announced on Oct 22 that it has signed an agreement with the Philippine Stock Exchange to explore offerings like depository receipts. This move aims to address low investor interest in US stocks listed via SGX's Singapore depository receipts programme.
items.title: SGX Group Signs Agreement to Explore Dual Listings with Philippine Stock Exchange

items.summary: Chua Ee Cheong, a practising doctor in Singapore, argues that while aesthetic treatments like Botox and dermal fillers are becoming mainstream, they must remain viewed as medical interventions rather than consumer goods. He cautions that marketing these procedures through promotional prices or social media trends risks overshadowing essential discussions about suitability and potential complications. The doctor emphasizes that medical consultations should provide objective assessments and honest discussions, sometimes recommending against treatment, rather than functioning as sales exercises. He urges patients to seek second opinions and feel comfortable declining procedures without pressure, ensuring practitioners maintain professional standards as these treatments become more accessible.
items.title: Doctor warns against treating aesthetic procedures as consumer products

items.summary: Singaporean pharmacists are expanding their role in preventive care, supporting initiatives like Healthier SG through smoking cessation and flu vaccinations. Since 2024, the Pharmaceutical Society of Singapore and NUS have offered health checks during Pharmacy Week, reaching over 330 residents by late June 2026. These efforts aim to extend years spent living well as Singaporeans age.
items.title: Pharmacists in Singapore Expand Preventive Care Roles

items.summary: The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas raised interest rates by a half-point to 5.5% on Oct 22, a move significantly larger than economist expectations. The central bank signaled readiness to tighten further to combat resurgent inflation, which reached 7.2% in September. Governor Eli Remolona cited urgent pressure from global oil shocks and a potential severe El Nino dry spell as drivers for the decisive action.
items.title: Philippines Central Bank Hikes Rates Sharply Amid Inflation Surge

items.summary: An article argues that India's Forest Rights Act (FRA) provides a framework for addressing land and resource conflicts surrounding new data centers. Citing a Google-Adani project in Visakhapatnam, the author highlights how local communities face socio-ecological costs without gaining promised benefits. The piece suggests adopting the FRA's bottom-up governance model, which empowers local institutions like the gram sabha, to ensure meaningful public consultation and protect community rights before land allocation. It calls for shifting from a land-acquisition model to one that recognizes pre-existing community claims.
items.title: India's Forest Rights Act Offers Lessons for Data Center Governance

items.summary: Perplexity and NVIDIA researchers introduced JOLT, a post-training method for language models that employs a joint teacher-student reinforcement learning approach. Unlike previous methods, JOLT trains a single model to act as both teacher and student, with the teacher receiving privileged information to provide feedback. The method was tested across five benchmarks, including MATH and AppWorld, where JOLT+ achieved the highest mean scores against baselines like GRPO. Specifically, JOLT+ improved AppWorld state-test pass rates by 9.9 points compared to GRPO. Additionally, JOLT required 6.5 times fewer processed training tokens than GRPO to reach matched accuracy on the MATH benchmark, offering significant computational efficiency.
items.title: Perplexity and NVIDIA Introduce JOLT for Efficient Language Model Training

items.summary: GitLab released security patches for a maximum-severity vulnerability, CVE-2026-110264, in its Regular Expression Compiler that allowed remote attackers to execute arbitrary code. The flaw stems from an integer overflow weakness and affects multiple versions of GitLab Community and Enterprise Editions. GitLab warned users to patch immediately, while watchdog Shadowserver tracks over 2,700 exposed instances.
items.title: GitLab Patches Critical Code Execution Flaw in Regular Expression Compiler

items.summary: Google and Voltus announced a new agreement to add one gigawatt of clean capacity through virtual power plants over the next three or four years, aiming to meet growing data center power needs in the PJM Interconnection region.
items.title: Google and Voltus Partner on Gigawatt Virtual Power Plant Deal

items.summary: Google is funding a 1 GW virtual power plant in the Mid-Atlantic to accelerate data center operations. The deal, a contract with Voltus extending through 2040, represents a significant expansion of Voltus's existing portfolio. Voltus CEO Dana Guernsey stated the agreement is designed to catalyze the market and prove the scalability of distributed energy resources, particularly batteries, which are expected to play a significant role in the project.
items.title: Google Signs Contract for 1 GW Virtual Power Plant with Voltus

items.summary: Iraq's government has eliminated customs duties on imported solar energy systems to support the transition to renewable energy and reduce costs. The Council of Ministers approved the measure following a proposal by Electricity Minister Ali Saadi Waheeb. Concurrently, the Ministry of Electricity finalized regulations for grid interconnection, while the Central Bank granted loans for solar projects. The move aims to accelerate solar adoption as the market gains momentum.
items.title: Iraq Eliminates Import Tariffs on Solar Systems to Boost Renewable Energy

items.summary: Record-high gasoline and diesel prices across Europe are accelerating a shift toward electric vehicles and hybrids. Data from the European Automobile Manufacturers' Association shows total car sales rose 10.2% in September 2026, driven by a 60% jump in battery electric vehicle sales and a 24% rise in plug-in hybrids. Conversely, gasoline and diesel car sales slumped by over 20% and 28.2% respectively.
items.title: Record Fuel Prices Drive EV Sales Surge in Europe

items.summary: Senior Congress leader Sonia Gandhi debuted on Instagram, sharing a preview of her upcoming autobiography, 'Belonging: A Journey of Love.' Published by HarperCollins India on November 10, the book follows a previous publishing dispute with Penguin Random House India regarding editorial changes.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi debuts on Instagram with new book preview

items.summary: Microsoft attributes a recent cyberattack targeting over 2,250 corporate cloud environments to the Storm-0940 group, which it alleges is China-aligned. The attackers utilized the ARTEX open-source AI framework to automate login attempts against trusted ConnectWise applications, reaching speeds of up to 2,900 attempts per minute. Consequently, more than 151,000 sign-ins failed, causing major impacts for some organizations.
items.title: Microsoft Accuses China-Linked Group of AI-Powered Cyberattacks on ConnectWise

items.summary: Quilombola communities in Pará, Brazil, have resisted displacement by palm oil companies producing biofuels. Josias Dias dos Santos describes decades of violence, including unprosecuted ambushes and decapitation of leaders. In 2022, the Acará community blockaded Brasil BioFuels (BBF), leading to court rulings that recognized their land rights and rejected most criminal charges against them. While BBF executives claim the land was legally acquired years ago, the community faces ongoing threats. By 2024, BBF declared bankruptcy, and new companies lease the land, yet the quilombolas maintain control over thousands of hectares despite uncertainty and fear.
items.title: Quilombolas in Brazil's Amazon Defend Land Against Biofuel Giants

items.summary: Tesla shares fell 5% in premarket trading after the company lowered its 2026 capital spending forecast to about $20 billion from more than $25 billion. The reduction follows lower-than-expected spending on AI and robotics in the third quarter, raising questions about investment pace for Musk's ambitions. J.P.Morgan analysts noted investors may have mixed feelings about the delay.
items.title: Tesla Shares Slide on Reduced Capital Spending Forecast

items.summary: Axel Springer stated it would welcome a European initiative to separate TikTok from Chinese ownership, mirroring a US deal involving President Donald Trump. A spokesperson confirmed the company's interest following a Financial Times report suggesting CEO Mathias Doepfner pitched the idea to the US Ambassador to France. Doepfner previously criticized TikTok as a propaganda machine and advocated for a European solution similar to the American model.
items.title: Axel Springer Open to Role in European TikTok Deal

items.summary: Chinese AI firm DeepSeek raised approximately $15 billion in a record financing round to compete with Western technology leaders. The Hangzhou-based company previously unveiled a cost-effective model challenging Silicon Valley standards. While seeking capital for international expansion, DeepSeek faces increased global regulatory scrutiny, with some US agencies banning its technology from government devices. Analysts suggest the funding sets the stage for an imminent public listing.
items.title: DeepSeek Secures Major Funding Amid Global Regulatory Scrutiny

items.summary: CEO Elon Musk stated that both SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees to discuss a potential merger. He noted that such a merger would require approval from 50% of shareholders. The report clarifies that NPR does not accept money for coverage or interviews, and any such requests do not represent the organization.
items.title: Elon Musk Says SpaceX and Tesla Considering Merger

items.summary: Research by Sophie Nottmeyer indicates that digital monitoring via GPS tracking resolves information frictions in Kenya's tractor rental market. Evidence from 1,200 GPS-tracked tractors shows that remote monitoring allows owners to send machines further from home, expanding their operational range by approximately 55 kilometres. This increased mobility leads to higher vegetation growth on serviced fields, suggesting real productivity gains. Nottmeyer estimates that while current adoption stands between 2% and 8%, fully resolving monitoring frictions could reduce misallocation by 16% and raise aggregate output by around 2%, offering a cost-effective alternative to fuel subsidies.
items.title: Digital Monitoring Expands Tractor Access in Kenya

items.summary: Research indicates that China's centralized procurement pilot, which guaranteed hospitals a fixed share of purchases for winning bidders, significantly reduced generic drug prices and marketing spending. Prices for covered medicines fell by approximately 40% compared to a control group, while sales revenue dropped by about 43%. Winning firms saw their product prices decrease by roughly 52% and marketing expenditures decline, evidenced by fewer job advertisements for marketing roles. The study suggests that securing sales through guaranteed volumes reduces the need for promotion and hidden payments, offering a mechanism to lower costs where enforcement of anti-kickback laws is difficult. However, the researchers note that their analysis covers short-run effects and does not measure health outcomes.
items.title: China's Centralized Procurement Cuts Drug Prices and Marketing

items.summary: Musk's public remarks on a potential SpaceX-Tesla merger have raised concerns among participants regarding shareholder scrutiny and potential delays. While special committees of independent directors have been formed to examine the deal, advisers are working to ensure Musk remains excluded from discussions. Legal experts note that the outcome may be uncertain due to Texas law, contrasting with the Delaware-based SolarCity precedent.
items.title: Musk's Comments Complicate SpaceX-Tesla Merger Talks

items.summary: IBM stock fell after the company reported net income of $2.19 billion, surpassing analyst expectations. While revenue and earnings beat estimates, the stock slipped. IBM raised its full-year free cash flow outlook to growth of more than $1 billion and maintained a 4%-5% revenue growth forecast. CEO Arvind Krishna attributed results to disciplined execution.
items.title: IBM Stock Slips Despite Beating Revenue and Earnings Estimates

items.summary: Despite high oil prices and political pressure from President Trump to increase drilling, Permian Basin operators like Diamondback Energy remain cautious. CEO Kaes Van't Hof notes that while prices are high, they attract scrutiny and potential regulation. Companies are prioritizing long-term financial stability over rapid expansion, having learned from past market crashes. Production growth remains modest, with many executives fearing a future price collapse. The region sees economic stability but anxiety about Washington's unpredictable policies, with only a minority of companies reporting increased business activity.
items.title: Texan Drillers Resist Pressure to Increase Production Amid Oil Price Surge

items.summary: A potential merger between SpaceX and Tesla faces significant political hurdles, particularly scrutiny from Beijing and potential conflict between President Donald Trump and Democrats. Elon Musk revived speculation, describing the combination as a good idea and noting committees are reviewing it. However, uniting a major aerospace contractor with a China-exposed manufacturer raises national security questions in Washington and Beijing, potentially creating obstacles beyond regulatory issues.
items.title: Political Concerns May Hinder SpaceX-Tesla Merger Prospects

items.summary: According to an anonymous source, the U.S. and Israel are preparing plans for a possible attack on Iran early next month, potentially occurring after the U.S. midterm elections and Israel's upcoming vote. NPR's Ruth Sherlock suggests these preparations might aim to pressure Iran into a diplomatic deal. Meanwhile, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is campaigning to topple Iran's regime and may use the threat of military action to form a unity government if election results remain uncertain. In other news, SpaceX and Tesla are exploring a merger that could amplify Elon Musk's influence and create one of the largest companies globally.
items.title: U.S. and Israel Plan Potential Iran Strike; SpaceX and Tesla Explore Merger

items.summary: Government websites across Europe became unavailable on Wednesday as operators patched two critical PHP vulnerabilities. The flaws could allow attackers to trigger memory corruption and code execution. Researchers at cybersecurity firms discovered the issues using AI tools, noting they had gone undetected for over a decade. Finland and the Dutch cybersecurity agency suspended services, while Britain's Oxford City Council temporarily shut down its site as a precaution. Patches were released Wednesday afternoon.
items.title: European Government Websites Shut Down Due to PHP Vulnerabilities

items.summary: At the 2026 Financial Street Forum, Zhang Ke, executive chairman of the Beijing Frontier Institute of Regulation and Supervision Technology, discussed AI's role in finance with CGTN. He described AI as a driver of the fifth industrial revolution but warned that reliance on path and data dependence poses risks. Zhang emphasized that while AI boosts efficiency, human oversight remains essential for accountability in critical financial decisions.
items.title: Zhang Ke Warns of AI Risks in Finance at 2026 Forum

items.summary: Mary Peltola, a pro-oil Democrat, campaigns for Alaska's Senate seat, highlighting high living costs in rural areas exacerbated by tariffs and the Iran conflict. She aims to be the first Democrat to win the seat in nearly two decades. Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan faces challenges from Peltola and a potential Republican primary challenger. The race is intense, with both candidates receiving significant support from outside groups. Trump has rallied behind Sullivan, while Peltola emphasizes the need for oil production to fund state services. The election outcome may take time due to Alaska's ranked-choice voting system.
items.title: Mary Peltola Campaigns in Alaska Amid Cost Crisis and Tariff Tensions

items.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met with Djibouti's Abdoulkader Houssein Omar in Beijing on October 21, 2026. Wang stated that China-Djibouti relations have maintained healthy momentum, citing deepened political trust and mutual benefits. He emphasized China's appreciation for Djibouti's adherence to the one-China principle and expressed willingness to deepen pragmatic cooperation. Omar reciprocated, noting Djibouti's commitment to mutual respect and readiness to enhance dialogue on international issues.
items.title: Chinese and Djibouti Foreign Ministers Meet in Beijing to Discuss Strategic Partnership

items.summary: Shaanbei Public School was founded in Yan'an, Shaanxi Province, in 1937 as a revolutionary university established following the Long March. It served as the predecessor to today's Renmin University of China. Long March veterans utilized their experience to train thousands for the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression. Mao Zedong praised the institution, stating, "China will not perish, for we have Shaanbei Public School!"
items.title: Shaanbei Public School Founded in Yan'an in 1937

items.summary: Authorities in South Korea have failed in a third attempt to rescue Bukangi, an endangered dusky shark trapped in a canal in Busan for nearly a month. The shark has become a viral sensation, attracting 1.6 million visitors to the city. Officials now hope the animal will find its own way back to the sea.
items.title: Authorities Fail to Rescue Trapped Shark in South Korean Port

items.summary: A report by the Migration Policy Institute indicates the Trump administration has failed to meet its goal of deporting one million people annually. In the first 18 months of his second term, the administration deported 980,000 people, a figure that exceeds removals under previous administrations but falls short of the target. While interior deportations have risen to about 19,000 monthly, the administration has not surpassed historical totals. The analysis notes that 69% of deportations involved border encounters, and voluntary departures have multiplied tenfold, though the total number of immigrants leaving remains below three million.
items.title: Trump Administration Misses Deportation Target Despite Increased Efforts

items.summary: A new analysis by energy think tank Ember indicates that electric vehicle fleets have displaced an estimated 200 million barrels of crude oil, valued at $20 billion (€17.82 billion) between March and August 2026. This shift has provided significant protection against rising oil prices driven by the conflict in the Middle East. While China accounted for the largest share of savings, six European countries combined saved nearly €2 billion. Analysts note that early investment in EVs has improved energy security and economic resilience, though environmental benefits depend on battery production and electricity sources.
items.title: European EVs Saved Billions in Oil Costs Amid Iran War Crisis

items.summary: Treasurer Jim Chalmers stated that business investment in Australia is growing more than twice as fast as previously forecast, driven by global investors viewing the nation as a stable opportunity. While acknowledging that Treasury expects higher unemployment and lower growth in the upcoming December budget update, Chalmers emphasized the investment boom as a positive indicator. Conversely, Reserve Bank Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser expressed pessimism regarding inflation, noting the outlook is materially worse than forecast. This economic tension has increased political pressure on the Albanese government, with opposition figures citing the government's spending habits as a cause for household financial strain.
items.title: Treasurer Chalmers highlights investment boom amid domestic economic concerns

items.summary: President Donald Trump's recent moves to ease economic pressure on Russia while increasing criticism of Ukraine have triggered bipartisan opposition in Congress. By lifting sanctions on Russian diesel exports and officials while calling for Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's replacement, Trump risks complicating his agenda following the upcoming midterm elections, according to the report.
items.title: Trump's Russia Policy Shifts Spark Congressional Backlash Ahead of Midterms

items.summary: Storm Adam triggered severe flooding in southern France, resulting in at least four deaths and one injury. Authorities found two women drowned in a cellar in the Bouches-du-Rhône region. Local media reported a 4x4 vehicle swept away by floodwaters. In eastern Spain, Storm Adam also caused flooding, killing at least three people. The Valencian government approved an aid package of €23.5m (£20m) for those affected.
items.title: Storm Adam Causes Flooding and Deaths in Southern France and Spain

items.summary: Go Vilnius proposes a leisurely marathon in Vilnius during Christmas 2026, allowing participants to walk or run at their own pace without registration. Routes range from 3km to 42.195km, passing through festive attractions. Eglė Girdzijauskaitė of Go Vilnius aims to counter the rush of the season by encouraging a slower pace through the city's historic sites.
items.title: Vilnius launches Europe's slowest marathon for festive season

items.summary: A recent landslide in South Solok district, Sumatra, killed four gold miners, marking the latest fatalities in the region's illegal mining sector. Authorities identified the victims and noted that mud and rocks prevented rescue efforts. This incident follows a similar May event that killed nine miners in the same province. Local environmental groups report over 50 deaths in the sector across Indonesia in the last 15 years, with one office recording 52 deaths. High global gold prices and geopolitical tensions are driving more people into dangerous, informal mining operations despite significant health and environmental risks.
items.title: Landslide Kills Four Miners in Indonesia's Illegal Gold Rush

items.summary: India Today analysis reveals the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) faced a significant decline in Instagram engagement between July and October. While the party's page saw an 80% drop in total volume, individual leaders like Abhijit Dipke experienced a smaller 30% fall. Conversely, opposition figures such as Rahul Gandhi and Union ministers saw varied results, with some gaining substantial engagement. The report suggests that CJP lost narrative ownership as opposition parties adopted similar causes, and the party's reduced posting frequency contributed to the decline. Despite the drop in page metrics, individual leader accounts retained more relative engagement compared to the party page.
items.title: Cockroach Janata Party Instagram Engagement Plummets as Opposition Gains Ground

items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang dismissed warnings that artificial intelligence could wipe out humanity as "cheap" attempts to grab headlines. Speaking in Berlin, he called such claims untrue and urged responsible optimism. While researchers like those at Anthropic have called for a slowdown, Huang advocates for full-speed development. He noted that US regulators are unlikely to intervene, and Nvidia pledged nearly $10 billion in European investments.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Dismisses AI Existential Risk Warnings as Cheap Headline Grabbing

items.summary: Apple has implemented a strict policy limiting online customers to a maximum of two iPhones per transaction. This cap applies to all current models, including the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo, and prevents purchasing more than two units regardless of model variety. The Times of India Tech confirmed the system blocks orders exceeding this limit, though physical stores remain unaffected. Apple suggests the measure targets scalpers, though no official statement was issued.
items.title: Apple Enforces Two-Unit iPhone Purchase Limit Online

items.summary: Hindu monk Swami Sarvapriyananda recounted late-night conversations with Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT, noting both described themselves as 'high functioning machines' without feelings. Speaking at the NDTV World Summit, the monk highlighted that researchers encouraged treating AIs as persons, a practice Rabbi Mois Navon also observed. The article notes that human-like conversation does not prove consciousness, leaving the question of AI moral agency unresolved.
items.title: Hindu Monk Recounts AI Chatbots Calling Themselves Machines During Anthropic Visit

items.summary: US President Donald Trump recalled suggesting to Google CEO Sundar Pichai that the Atlantic Ocean be renamed 'Trump Ocean' on Google Maps. Pichai reportedly dismissed the idea, stating oceans cover multiple countries and cannot be changed. Trump later clarified the suggestion was a joke, though he previously proposed renaming other geographical features, causing diplomatic tensions.
items.title: Trump Recalls Requesting Atlantic Ocean Be Renamed on Google Maps

items.summary: Sonia Gandhi made her Instagram debut on Thursday to promote her upcoming memoir, 'Belonging: A Journey of Love,' scheduled for release on November 10. In her first post, she described the book as a story of love, duty, and belonging. The launch follows a publishing dispute between HarperCollins India and Penguin Random House India regarding the book's domestic publication.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi Launches Instagram Account Ahead of Memoir Release

items.summary: Arya.ag announced its expansion into the Himachal apple value chain, bringing technology and finance capabilities to key growing regions. The company plans to use AI grading and controlled atmosphere storage to improve supply consistency. This move addresses the unique post-harvest needs of apples, distinct from their grain commerce operations, aiming to support growers and buyers throughout the season.
items.title: Arya.ag Enters Himachal Apple Market with New Technology

items.summary: A YES Bank report indicates the Reserve Bank of India faces rising inflation risks, with projections reaching 6 per cent. While economic growth remains resilient at 7.8 per cent, the bank suggests maintaining an interest rate gap with G7 nations to attract foreign capital. Consequently, YES Bank forecasts a cumulative 50 basis point repo rate increase by February.
items.title: YES Bank Report Highlights RBI Inflation and Rate Gap Concerns

items.summary: Axel Springer proposed acquiring a stake in TikTok's European operations, a pitch initiated by CEO Mathias Dopfner during a meeting with US Ambassador Charles Kushner. While the proposal reached European Commission officials, it failed to gain traction. ByteDance dismissed the idea, stating no formal acquisition discussions occurred. The move mirrors US restructuring efforts but differs from Springer's previous media acquisitions.
items.title: Axel Springer Proposes TikTok European Stake Rejected by ByteDance

items.summary: Economists anticipate the Reserve Bank of India will raise interest rates in December following October MPC minutes signaling tighter policy due to inflation risks. SBI Research predicts a potential 50 basis point increase, while RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra highlighted sector-wide inflation concerns. The rupee appreciated 1.5% against the dollar, though global oil prices continue to pressure bond markets.
items.title: Economists Anticipate RBI Rate Hike Amid Inflation Concerns

items.summary: Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan ordered legal action against a fake WhatsApp channel impersonating his office. The channel circulated misleading information and unrelated content. An FIR is being initiated against those responsible. The Deputy Chief Minister's Office stated that misuse of government identity will not be tolerated and urged the public to rely only on official handles for authentic updates.
items.title: AP Deputy CM Pawan Kalyan Orders Legal Action Against Fake WhatsApp Channel

items.summary: Former Congress chief Sonia Gandhi made her Instagram debut, sharing a first look at her memoir 'Belonging: A Journey of Love,' set for release on November 10. At 79, she received copies in New Delhi and described the book as a story of love and duty. Published by HarperCollins India and Alfred A. Knopf, the memoir reflects on her life and India's political changes over six decades.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi debuts on Instagram with memoir 'Belonging'

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that India and the United States are very close to finalizing a trade agreement, with only a few issues remaining. Speaking on The Business Today Show and in an exclusive interview with India Today, Rubio emphasized the pact's aim to provide business certainty. He also noted Washington's readiness to help prevent conflict between India and Pakistan.
items.title: US Secretary Rubio Says India-US Trade Deal Near Completion

items.summary: Neha Bora, president of the All India Students' Association, appeared before the Delhi High Court to challenge a police notice directing her to execute a peace bond. The notice, issued under Section 126 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, alleged she instigated a demonstration at Central Park on October 16. Bora argued the notice was factually incorrect and vague, stating she called for a peaceful gathering at Mandi House instead. She was briefly detained on October 16 before being released. The court is scheduled to pass an order on Friday evening regarding her plea.
items.title: Neha Bora Challenges Police Peace Bond Order in Delhi High Court

items.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav met jailed leader Azam Khan at Rampur jail ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh elections. Yadav alleged the BJP government pursued a political vendetta against Khan's family through false cases and undermined institutions linked to him. The meeting focused on electoral strategy and discussing 403 Assembly constituencies, with Yadav reaffirming the party's primary objective of defeating the BJP.
items.title: Akhilesh Yadav Meets Jailed Azam Khan and Accuses BJP of Injustice

items.summary: Adani Green Energy shares fell 4% following Q2 results showing a 45% year-over-year revenue increase to Rs 4,019 crore. EBITDA surged 51% to Rs 3,835 crore with a margin of 92%. Jefferies retained a 'Buy' rating with a target of Rs 1,695, citing attractive valuations. JM Financial maintained an 'Add' rating at Rs 1,374. Analysts note rising power demand and potential El Niño conditions as growth drivers despite interest rate concerns.
items.title: Adani Green Energy Shares Fall After Q2 Results and Brokerage Ratings

items.summary: International Gemological Institute Ltd. reported robust growth for the quarter and half-year ended September 30, 2026. Consolidated revenue rose 31% year-on-year to Rs 398 crore, while profit after tax jumped 43% to Rs 185.8 crore. CEO Tehmasp Printer attributed the results to healthy demand trends and strong operational execution across grading and certification services for diamonds and gemstones.
items.title: IGI Shares Surge on Strong Q2 Profit and Revenue Growth

items.summary: A chemical used to make tyres last longer breaks down into 6PPD-quinone, a toxin linked to mass salmon deaths in U.S. urban streams. With vehicle sales rising in India, experts warn the problem could grow, but no data exists on toxin levels in Indian road dust or water bodies. Experts call for regulating 6PPD and better stormwater management, noting that poor drainage and sewage-laden drains in Indian cities could carry the toxin into rivers. While a 2022 global study found Kolkata ranked first in diphenylguanidine concentration, it did not report quantified data on 6PPD-Q.
items.title: Experts warn of unmeasured toxic tyre chemical in India

items.summary: This commentary argues that Christopher Columbus' arrival in the New World initiated global biogeographical shifts and ecological disruption. The author contends that his voyages triggered an unprecedented exchange of organisms, leading to the spread of invasive species and pathogenic microorganisms that devastated indigenous populations and agriculture. The text identifies the post-Columbus period as an era of rapid, irreversible biosphere changes, noting that the past 500 years have seen the most significant alterations to Earth's ecosystems. The author, R.J. Ranjit Daniels, suggests these changes have tested the biosphere's resilience and exceeded its capacity to absorb disturbances.
items.title: Commentary on Columbus' voyages accelerating Earth's biodiversity homogenisation

items.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk held bilateral talks in New Delhi to strengthen strategic cooperation. The leaders agreed to expand collaboration in defence, space, nuclear energy, and critical minerals, inviting Polish companies to participate in joint projects. They also reaffirmed their commitment to peace in Ukraine and West Asia. Both nations aim to double their bilateral trade by 2030, leveraging the upcoming India-EU Free Trade Agreement. The visit, Tusk's second as prime minister, underscores a shared legacy of humanity and a desire for deeper economic and technological partnerships amid global uncertainty.
items.title: India and Poland deepen strategic ties in defence and space

items.summary: India condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi civil infrastructure, including strikes on King Fahd and Dammam airports, following the death of an Indian national and injuries to others. The external affairs ministry expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia and called for the cessation of such attacks. India is facilitating the return of stranded Indian pilgrims through airlines and tour operators, with thousands having already returned. The government also extended welfare assistance to affected nationals while urging a return to dialogue and diplomacy in the escalating conflict between Iran-backed Houthis and the Saudi-backed Yemeni government.
items.title: India Condemns Houthi Strikes on Saudi Infrastructure and Aids Stranded Pilgrims

items.summary: The Central Information Commission directed the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights to actively monitor child abuse complaints rather than merely forwarding them. Citing an RTI appeal regarding alleged physical abuse of disabled children in Gulbarga, the CIC emphasized that the statutory body must ensure appropriate follow-up and provide detailed action reports. The commission noted that general communications were insufficient and ordered a point-by-point response with records of any inspections or inquiries conducted.
items.title: CIC Orders NCPCR to Monitor Child Abuse Complaints Effectively

items.summary: In the first T20I between India and New Zealand in Christchurch on October 22, Sanju Samson scored 67 off 33 balls to anchor India's record chase of 226. Despite a middle-overs collapse where India lost three wickets for seven runs, cameos from captain Shreyas Iyer (42) and Naman Dhir (42 not out off 15) secured a four-wicket win with two balls remaining. New Zealand posted 225/8, their highest total on home soil, but India's lower-order resilience proved decisive.
items.title: Samson leads India to record T20I chase victory over New Zealand

items.summary: Neha Bora, president of AISA, challenged a Delhi High Court notice requiring her to furnish a Rs 10,000 personal bond and maintain peace. Her counsel argued the notice was factually incorrect and vague, citing her peaceful participation in protests. Bora denied involvement in the Cockroach Janta Party's protest call. The court is hearing her plea against the Special Executive Magistrate's order.
items.title: Neha Bora Challenges Peace Bond in Delhi High Court
